name: Anterior Uveitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Standard Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Anterior Uveitis

criteria.description: Presence of inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber on slit-lamp examination
Detection of keratic precipitates on the corneal endothelium
Protein flare in the anterior chamber indicating blood-aqueous barrier disruption
Symptoms such as eye redness, photophobia, and ocular pain

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anterior chamber inflammatory cells and keratic precipitates with clinical symptoms consistent with anterior uveitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by slit-lamp biomicroscopy findings.

searchTerms: white blood cells in eye chamber
inflammation causing flare in eye chamber
protein flare in front eye chamber
cloudy fluid in eye anterior chamber

occasional.symptomName: Hypopyon (layering of white blood cells in anterior chamber)
searchTerms: eye infection with white cell layering

rare.symptomName: Posterior synechiae (adhesions between iris and lens)

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in systemic disease-associated cases
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing anterior chamber cells and flare
Ultrasound biomicroscopy may be used in severe cases
genetic: Association with HLA-B27 allele in many cases
other: Response to corticosteroid therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Corneal dendritic ulcers visible on fluorescein staining
Typically unilateral with corneal epithelial involvement
Severe pain and vision loss with hypopyon
History of recent intraocular surgery or trauma
Superficial redness without anterior chamber inflammation
Mild discomfort rather than severe pain

redFlags: Elevated intraocular pressure indicating secondary glaucoma
references: Jabs DA, Nussenblatt RB, Rosenbaum JT. Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature for Reporting Clinical Data. Am J Ophthalmol. 2005.
Nussenblatt RB. The natural history of uveitis. Int Ophthalmol. 1990.
Rosenbaum JT, Dick AD. Uveitis: Fundamentals and Clinical Practice. Elsevier, 2018.
